start_repo_body_a: A repository is a list of extensions that someone else keeps. tsundoku doesn't name one.
start_repo_body_b: Ask the friend who gave you tsundoku
start_repo_body_c: for theirs, or search the web for one. Paste its address here: it says what it holds before anything is installed.
start_holds_novels_repo: AN LNREADER PLUGIN REPOSITORY · ENDS IN {file}
start_ext_body: An extension is one source to browse and read from: a site, in a language. Your repository lists them. Pick one in AVAILABLE, and it's one search away.
start_library_body_a: Coming from Mihon, Aniyomi or LNReader? Make a backup in the app, then choose the file here. On a paired phone it can be done from the phone itself: the backup is usually in
start_library_files: FILES INSTEAD · EPUBS, AND DOWNLOADED CHAPTERS
start_wifi_body: Switch it on and scan the code with the phone's camera. The phone has to be on this same Wi-Fi.
start_wifi_cannot: NO OFFLINE CHAPTERS, NO APP INSTALL
start_tailscale_body: A free private network between your own devices. Everything works, offline chapters too. It needs a password and four steps.
start_tailscale_where_a: THE STEPS ARE IN README.TXT, BESIDE TSUNDOKU
start_empty_lede: Four things to set up, in any order, then three to read your first series. Each step ticks itself when it's done, and this list stays here until they are.
start_page_title_open: Set up, then a first read.
start_page_title_finished: Everything is set up, or skipped.

start_page_kept: THE SAME LIST ON EVERY DEVICE · TICKS AND SKIPS ARE KEPT ON THE COMPUTER
first_lede: Search your sources for something to read, or browse one. Read it straight away, or ADD a series to keep it here.
first_empty_lede: No sources and nothing imported. Files in the library folder appear after a scan; GET STARTED still opens from HELP.
setup_intro: Choose a password for tsundoku. You'll use it to sign in on this computer and, later, on your phone.
setup_none_body: Anyone who uses this computer can open tsundoku, and everything in it. Nothing else can reach it: to read on your phone, you'll set a password first.
setup_none_later: You can set one any time in {settings}, under DEVICES.
setup_error_here: set tsundoku up on the computer it runs on
login_pair_once: A CODE SIGNS IN ONE PHONE, ONCE
login_pair_remedy: ON THE COMPUTER: {settings} › {devices} › NEW CODE, THEN SCAN IT
login_unconfigured_body: TSUNDOKU_TOKEN is not set. The server refuses to authenticate without one: the workstation has no firewall running, so an unauthenticated library would be reachable from the whole LAN.
login_code_only_label: ONLY A CODE SIGNS IN HERE
login_code_only_body: tsundoku on the computer has no password, so a phone signs in by scanning its code: on the computer, {settings} › {devices} › WI-FI.
login_label_or_password: OR SIGN IN WITH THE PASSWORD
login_label_or_token: OR SIGN IN WITH THE TOKEN
login_forgot_a: Forgot it? On the computer tsundoku runs on, open the Start menu and choose RESET TSUNDOKU PASSWORD (on Linux, run
login_forgot_b: ). Then choose a new one here.
welcome_works_body: Reading, browsing, search, downloads, and every setting.
welcome_note: TAILSCALE GIVES THE PHONE ALL OF IT · THE README ON THE COMPUTER SAYS HOW
welcome_back_body: In the browser's menu, Add to Home screen. It's a shortcut to this address: if the address changes, scan a new code.
nav_rescan_reads: READS THE LIBRARY FOLDER ON THE WORKSTATION AGAIN.
nav_rescan_new: NEW SERIES APPEAR ON NEW AS THEY ARE FOUND.
nav_rescan_keeps: NOTHING IS REMOVED: WHAT IS HERE STAYS AS IT IS.
nav_rescan_took: THE LAST SCAN TOOK ABOUT {n} MIN.
nav_rescan_took_short: THE LAST SCAN TOOK UNDER A MINUTE.
tv_servers_forget_prose: This TV stops knowing {address} and drops its pairing there. To come back, add it again and type six digits from that computer.
tv_servers_forget_devices: THE COMPUTER LISTS THIS TV IN 08 — DEVICES UNTIL IT IS SIGNED OUT THERE
update_app_say: UPDATE downloads it, checks it was signed by tsundoku's release key, and hands it to Android, which asks you to confirm. Your library is on your computer, so it stays as it is.
update_app_permission: ALLOW INSTALLS FROM TSUNDOKU, THEN COME BACK
update_app_installing_meta: MATCHES THE RELEASE KEY · ANDROID INSTALLS IT
update_app_installing_say: Confirm on Android's own screen. The app opens again on the new version.
update_say_install: UPDATE downloads it and installs it. tsundoku closes for about a minute and opens again by itself, and this page comes back on its own. Your library stays as it is.
update_step_3: Start tsundoku from the new folder, then delete the old one. Your library stays where it is.
update_note_lead: LATER · ASKED AGAIN TOMORROW · IT WAITS IN
update_failed_say: tsundoku {version} is still running, as it was. TRY AGAIN downloads it afresh.
update_downloading_say: Keep reading if you like: HIDE closes this, and the library's band keeps count.
update_installing_meta: MATCHES THE RELEASE KEY · TSUNDOKU CLOSES NOW
update_installing_say: It opens again by itself in about a minute, and this page reloads onto it.
update_opening_say: Nothing to do here. If it takes more than a few minutes, start tsundoku from the Start menu: your library is untouched.
help_start_short_1: Seven steps in two parts: four to set up, in any order, then three to read your first series.
help_start_short_2: Each one ticks itself when it is done; SKIP any of them.
help_start_short_3: The list stays on the empty library, and here, until every step is done or skipped.
help_reading_meta: TAP, SWIPE, KEYS · THE STRIP · FULL SCREEN · ZOOM
help_reading_short_1: Tap an edge or swipe to turn. In R→L, the left edge goes forward.
help_reading_short_2: A tap in the middle shows the controls; a double tap zooms.
help_reading_short_3: SETTINGS ↑ in the controls opens the reading settings. FULL SCREEN hides the browser's bars.
help_reading_turning_edges_what: A tap on the left or right edge turns the page, the way the book reads.
help_reading_turning_swipe_what: Drag the page sideways to turn it; let go early and it stays.
help_reading_turning_middle_what: Shows the controls at the top and bottom. Tap again and they go.
help_reading_turning_keys_what: On a computer: ← and → turn, ↑ and ↓ move a screen in the strip, Ctrl with ↑ or ↓ nudges a little.
help_reading_strip_para_1: Manhwa read as one long strip: scroll, and the next chapter follows on. A mouse wheel and the arrow keys glide rather than jump.
help_reading_strip_para_2: In {settings} › {reading}, CHAPTERS can STOP AT THE END instead, with a button to go on, and TO THE TOP adds a button back to the chapter's first page.
help_reading_screen_para_1: FULL SCREEN, in the controls, hides the browser's bars on Android and computers; an iPhone's browser doesn't allow it.
help_reading_screen_para_2: A double tap zooms into a page, and pinching zooms too; a zoomed page pans under your finger and turns from its edges.
help_downloading_short_1: Extensions add sources, and come from a repository: ask whoever gave you tsundoku for one.
help_downloading_short_2: {browse} searches those sources. A series opens there and reads online, without being added.
help_downloading_short_3: + ADD puts it in your library. Its DOWNLOAD row downloads it, and FOLLOW keeps up.
help_downloading_extensions_para_1: Sources come from extensions, and extensions come from repositories. tsundoku ships none. Ask whoever gave you tsundoku for a repository's address, or search for one: Mihon, Aniyomi and LNReader repositories all work.
help_downloading_extensions_para_2: Paste the address in {extensions} › {repositories}. It says what the repository holds before anything is installed; then pick the sources you read from in {available}.
help_downloading_extensions_para_3: {extensions} lives in {browse}, beside the sources it gives. {settings} › 07 — BROWSE has a row that opens it too, with how many are installed and how many have updates.
help_downloading_online_para: Open a series from {browse} and read: each chapter comes from the source as you turn. Nothing is kept, and {history} remembers where you stopped. + ADD adds it whenever you decide.
help_downloading_download_add_what: Puts the series in your library, its chapters listed. No files yet.
help_downloading_download_first_what: Downloads the next ten you haven't read. After that it says NEXT 10.
help_downloading_download_all_what: Every chapter you haven't read. It asks first, and says how much room it takes.
help_downloading_download_follow_what: New chapters download by themselves when the source publishes them.
help_downloading_download_para: A series you haven't added has the DOWNLOAD row too: it asks first, since downloading adds it to your library.
help_downloading_queue_para: Downloads run on the computer tsundoku runs on, in the order you asked. {downloads} shows what's under way and what failed, with RETRY. A chapter that's in reads while the rest wait.
help_phone_short_1: At home: WI-FI › ON on the computer, then scan its code with the phone's camera.
help_phone_short_2: Over Wi-Fi the phone reads, browses and downloads, but can't keep chapters offline.
help_phone_short_3: For everything, anywhere: Tailscale, on the computer and the phone.
help_phone_wifi_para_1: On the computer, {settings} › {devices} › WI-FI › ON shows a code. Scan it with the phone's camera, on the same Wi-Fi, and the phone opens tsundoku signed in. A code works once, for ten minutes; NEW CODE makes another.
help_phone_wifi_para_2: Typing the address works too, with your password. Switch WI-FI off on a café's or a dorm's network: anyone on the same Wi-Fi reaches the sign-in page.
help_phone_wifi_para_3: Nothing opens on the phone? Then something on the computer keeps it out. Windows asks once, in a window of its own: allow tsundoku on private networks. Linux asks nothing: a firewall there (ufw, firewalld) drops the phone in silence. {settings} › {devices} › WI-FI names the port and gives the line to copy for your home network.
help_phone_wifi_works_what: Reading, browsing, searching, downloading, every setting.
help_phone_wifi_doesnt_what: Keeping chapters offline, installing tsundoku as an app, keeping the screen awake.
help_phone_tailscale_para: Tailscale is a free private network between your own devices. Over it the phone gets everything, offline chapters included, from anywhere. tsundoku needs a password first ({settings} › {devices}).
help_phone_tailscale_step_1: Install Tailscale on this computer and the phone, signed in to the same account.
help_phone_tailscale_step_2: In Tailscale's admin console, on the DNS page, turn on MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates.
help_phone_tailscale_step_3: Add the line TSUNDOKU_SERVE=https to the .env in your data folder.
help_phone_tailscale_step_4: Start tsundoku again and open the address its window prints, on the phone too.
help_updates_meta: HOW A NEW VERSION ARRIVES · THE LIBRARY STAYS
help_updates_short_1: When a new version is out, tsundoku says so when you open it, and in {settings} › {devices} › UPDATES.
help_updates_short_2: UPDATE installs it: tsundoku closes for a minute and opens again.
help_updates_short_3: Your library, your settings and your password stay as they are.
help_updates_shows_para: tsundoku asks its releases for a new version once a day. When there is one, the library opens with what's new, UPDATE and LATER; LATER asks again the next day. The UPDATES row keeps it, with CHECK to ask now.
help_updates_unzipped_para: Where UPDATE isn't offered (Linux, or Windows from the zip), DOWNLOAD fetches the new version. Unpack it beside this one and start tsundoku from the new folder; delete the old folder once the new one runs.
help_backups_meta: A MIHON BACKUP · THE LIBRARY FOLDER
help_backups_short_1: Your own files go in the library folder: a Mihon backup under Mihon/autobackup, EPUBs anywhere.
help_backups_short_2: RESCAN reads the folder again; new series appear as they are found.
help_backups_short_3: Your library and its reading are kept in the data folder, beside tsundoku.
help_backups_folder_mihon_what: A backup (.tachibk) under Mihon/autobackup: the series, its chapters and its reading. Downloads beside it are not imported.
help_backups_folder_para: START SCAN on the empty library, or RESCAN in the sidebar or in {more} after it asks, reads the folder again. /scan in the search does too.
help_report_meta: SAVE A REPORT · WHAT'S IN IT · WHO GETS IT
help_report_short_1: {settings} › {library} › REPORT › SAVE writes one text file about what went wrong.
help_report_short_2: It never holds your password or tokens, and your folders are written as <data> and <user>.
help_report_short_3: Nothing is sent by itself: send the file to whoever gave you tsundoku.
help_report_save_para: The report holds the version, the system, whether Wi-Fi and updates are on, whether the engine answers, and the last lines of tsundoku's logs. Read it before you send it, if you like: it's plain text.
help_not_here_updates_a: NOT ON THIS INSTALL · IT HAS NO UPDATER
help_not_here_updates_b: THIS ONE IS UPDATED WHERE IT'S BUILT · BELOW IS HOW AN INSTALL FROM TSUNDOKU'S RELEASES GETS ONE

help_still_stuck_body: Save a report and send it to whoever gave you tsundoku.

settings_fw_found_body: Run this in a terminal on this computer to let a phone on {subnet} in. It asks for your password: tsundoku never runs it for you.
settings_fw_commands_body: Run the one for your firewall in a terminal on this computer, to let a phone on {subnet} in. It asks for your password: tsundoku never runs it for you.
settings_fw_windows: WINDOWS WILL ASK TO LET TSUNDOKU THROUGH ITS FIREWALL · ALLOW IT ON PRIVATE NETWORKS
settings_fw_windows_fix_1: Open Windows Security › Firewall & network protection › Allow an app through firewall, and tick Private beside tsundoku.
settings_fw_windows_fix_2: Then set this Wi-Fi to Private: Settings › Network & internet › Wi-Fi › this network › Private network.
